LESSON: SIGN READING 7.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: INTERPRETATION AND EVALUATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Sign Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should you give the correct interpretation of a text? 2. How can you interpret a text correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme in readiness for intensive reading,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. distinguish between reading for interpretation and reading for evaluation for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. interpret a reading text for lifelong learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. summarise information in a reading text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Digital literacy: Learner develops technology skills as he/she sign reads and summarises digital texts related to the theme

Values:
Respect: Is fostered as the learner forms own judgments on texts read or sign read.

Link to other subjects

The languages, Mathematics and Integrated Science all emphasise the need for good skills in interpretation and evaluation.
